recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. No FHIR core source follow-up is recommended for FHIR-18280; future jurisdiction expansion failures should be handled in THO/UTG or terminology publication tooling.
issue_request: FHIR-18280 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-I issue raised against STU3 and applied for STU3. It reported that the Jurisdiction ValueSet expansion failed with an unsupported urn:iso:std:iso:3166:-2 code system error, with a resolution to add support before normative publication and a Jira comment saying it was fixed.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly mentioning FHIR-18280 was found. The issue followed the historical addition of ISO 3166 Part 2 subdivision codes to source/terminologies/valueset-jurisdiction.xml, so the application appears to have been terminology-server/publication tooling support rather than a Jira-tagged source hunk.
additional_context: Related no-change audits for FHIR-14695 and FHIR-20375 are already on the combined branch. FHIR-31537 later resolved no-change because the current build expanded successfully, and UP-521 moved the Jurisdiction ValueSet CLD to THO at http://terminology.hl7.org/ValueSet/jurisdiction after core R5 deprecated it. Current core source no longer contains source/terminologies/valueset-jurisdiction.xml; active source bindings use the THO URL.
reconciliation: Made no source changes. The current core build-scoped source is already correct: authoritative bindings point to THO, the old core jurisdiction value set source is absent by later source evolution, and checked R5/THO publication pages render expansion content with urn:iso:std:iso:3166:-2 and without the reported unable-to-expand text.
